additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) is characterized by an uninterrupted period of illness during which there is a major mood episode (manic or mixed, and often depressive as well) concurrent with symptoms that meet Criterion A for schizophrenia. There must be at least a two-week period of psychotic symptoms (such as delusions or hallucinations) without prominent mood symptoms, distinguishing it from mood disorders with psychotic features, while mood episodes are present for the majority of the total duration of the illness. The bipolar type features manic episodes and may include major depressive episodes across the course. The disorder typically leads to significant social and occupational impairment, and its course can be episodic with partial or full remissions, often complicated by stress, substance use, and nonadherence to treatment.

patient.stressor: Fifteen months ago, Thomas’s long‑time executive retired and the company underwent a major reorganization, leaving him reporting to a new, younger leader while simultaneously taking on expanded coordination duties across multiple departments. The shift disrupted the structured routines he had cultivated for years and added evening events and cross‑time‑zone meetings that encroached on his art activities, hiking, and mentoring at the community center. Over the next year, colleagues saw his reliability and polished demeanor give way to disorganized scheduling, missed follow‑through on projects, and increasingly unusual comments during meetings, while at home his spouse noticed abrupt changes in his energy, sleep, and engagement with family and community events. After Thomas showed up unannounced at the office on a weekend insisting he needed to "document a hidden pattern" in company communications and his supervisor found him confused and unable to account for recent mistakes, HR contacted his spouse, who brought him to a psychiatric evaluation when it was clear his functioning had seriously deteriorated.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve been seeing and hearing things at work and at home that no one else seems to notice, and it’s starting to scare me.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: For months now I’ve been convinced that the emails and calendar invites going around the company are coded messages about me, like my new boss and people in other departments are quietly coordinating to test me or push me out, even when my wife and coworkers tell me it’s just normal office stuff.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: At the office and at home I keep hearing my name whispered from behind me and a man’s voice commenting on my work or warning me about “them,” and sometimes I see shadowy figures standing in the doorway or in the hallway that vanish when I look straight at them, and it’s gotten to the point where I can’t tell if I’m losing my mind or everyone else is missing something huge.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Outside of these high-energy spells, most days I just sit in my home office staring at the computer, feeling flat and blank, ignoring calls from friends and skipping the art group and hikes I used to love because I can’t seem to make myself care enough to get up and go.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I’ll go from feeling on top of the world and weirdly giddy—like I’m the only one who really understands how everything connects—to snapping at my wife and coworkers over tiny things, slamming doors or firing off sharp emails because I suddenly feel like everyone is against me or wasting my time.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: When I’m in that revved-up mode, I’ll stay at my desk or pace the house all night starting spreadsheets, reorganizing files, sketching out big “communication systems” for the whole company and rewriting policies in my head, bouncing from task to task without actually finishing anything because I feel too wired to sit still.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: There are stretches where I honestly believe I’m the only person in the organization who can see the bigger pattern in all the communications, like I’ve been given this special ability to decode it and that senior leadership will eventually recognize me as the one who can fix everything if I just push hard enough.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: Lately I can go two or three nights sleeping only a couple of hours, sometimes just dozing in my chair, and I wake up feeling charged and sure I don’t really need more sleep because my mind is racing with ideas I’m convinced I have to act on right away.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: Once I start talking about what I’m noticing—like the supposed patterns in emails or how meetings are connected—I can’t seem to stop; I jump from one thought to the next so fast that people cut me off or look confused, but I feel this pressure in my chest to keep explaining before the ideas disappear.

add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_and_manic_episode_occ: When I’m in those super-charged phases, barely sleeping and racing around with big plans for overhauling the company’s communication system, that’s also when the whispers get loudest and the shadowy figures seem to show up most, like the energy and the strange experiences are happening at the same time.
add_requirements.manic_episode_is_present_for_the_majorit: Looking back over this past year or so, I feel like I’ve spent more time revved up—talking fast, sleeping very little, chasing big ideas about my special role at work—than in the flatter, drained periods in between.
add_requirements.delusions_and_hallucinations_occur_for_2: There was a stretch earlier this year when my mood felt pretty neutral—no big highs or crashes—but I was still hearing my name whispered and was sure the emails were coded about me, even though my energy was low and I wasn’t buzzing with ideas like during my manic spells.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over the past several months I’ve missed deadlines, had projects taken away from me, stopped going to my art group and hikes, and my spouse has had to step in with HR and manage bills and appointments because I can’t keep my work or home responsibilities straight anymore.
add_requirements.duration: Ever since the reorganization about fifteen months ago, these swings in mood along with the strange experiences at work and home have been building and never really gone away.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: For roughly the past ten months, I’ve been dealing pretty steadily with the whispers, the shadowy figures, and the belief that company messages are secretly about me.
add_requirements.manic_episode_duration: For almost the whole past year, with only brief breaks, I’ve had these amped-up periods where I sleep very little, feel unusually important, and throw myself into grand plans for fixing the company’s systems.
